newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says convicted hijacker among sabotage group.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says convicted hijacker among sabotage group.

text.p: A Sudanese government newspaper said on Wednesday that a Sudanese convicted in Egypt for hijacking a plane was among a group of people arrested in Sudan for planning to assassinate Sudanese politicians.

The man, Adel Mahjoub, received a one-year suspended sentence in Egypt in 1995 for hijacking a Sudanese plane to the south Egyptian town of Luxor in April 1994. A superior court had reduced the sentence from 15 years with hard labour.

The newspaper quoted Mahjoub as saying that in fact he never faced trial and the Egyptian authorities then allowed him to join a Sudanese opposition group, which trained him in explosives and assassination techniques.

Relations between Egypt and Sudan have been poor for years, especially since Egypt accused the Sudanese government of helping the Islamist militants who tried to kill Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Addis Ababa in 1995. Sudan denies it.
Egypt had turned down a Sudanese request that it extradite Mahjoub for the hijacking and the superior court decided that he qualified for lenient treatment.
His lawyer said the aim of the hijacking was to seek asylum in Egypt from political and economic conditions in Sudan.

The newspaper quoted Mahjoub as saying he joined an opposition group led by Brigadier Abdelaziz Khaled, a former army officer who now commands rebel forces in northeastern Sudan, close to the border with Eritrea.

"He managed to infiltrate into Sudan with quantities of explosives. He was waiting for the zero hour to implement the mission he was entrusted with," the newspaper added. One of his missions was to blow up the Sudanese parliament, it said.
In comments published on Monday a Sudanese minister said the people arrested were Communist Party members backed by Eritrea.
